newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay admits to "psychological" banking crisis.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay admits to "psychological" banking crisis.

text.p: Paraguay's government admitted Wednesday there is a financial crisis in the country, but said it is caused more by depositor anxiety than by a real breakdown in the banking system.
"Objectively speaking there is no crisis. Psychologically speaking, yes, there is a big crisis," Hermes Gomez Ginard, the president of Paraguay's central bank, told a parliamentary commission.
"There is a crisis when the whole system is bad, which is not the case now. Only two of 33 banks in the system have problems," Ginard said.
But last week the government sent an emergency law to Congress aimed at controlling a run on deposits by savers.

The law came after the authorities took control of Banco Union, the country's largest private nationally-owned bank, and Ahorros Paraguayos, a savings and loan institution linked to Union. Another bank, Banco de Inversiones, was also put under control for the same reasons.

The institutions were taken over due to liquidity problems. Union has $190 million in deposits, making it the third largest holder of public deposits, and the biggest in private corporate deposits in the country.

Authorities are estimating the cost of bailing out the banks could go as high as $350 million. The central bank is committed by law to guarantee deposits of up to $2,300. ((-- Jose Maria Amarilla, Asuncion Newsroom, 595 21 444527))
